body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Background ranges are not the screenshot editor's ranges (confidence high)**

Section 6.1 gives padding 0–160, radius 0–48 and shadow 0–64. Failure 17 (line 133) and section 6.4 (line 434) say the values are clamped to "the screenshot editor's ranges" and use "same sliders". ADR 0049 decision 1 says the same. The real ranges are `PADDING_RANGE` 0–96, `RADIUS_RANGE` 0–28 and `SHADOW_RANGE` 0–100 (`apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/screenshots/beautify/backgrounds.ts:133-135`). `shadowCss` also reads shadow on a 0–100 scale (`backgrounds.ts:113-121`). As written, the parser and the reused `BeautifyPanel` would disagree: a 0–100 shadow slider would get clamped to 64, or the panel would need different ranges. Pick one rule, either the screenshot ranges or ranges specific to video, and say it in both the spec and the ADR.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: `bg = none` with padding/radius/shadow > 0 is left undefined, and the preview and export would disagree (confidence high)**

Decision 13 (line 55) adds `bg1` when `bg ≠ none` **or** padding/radius/shadow ≠ 0. So `hasBackground` can be true with `bg: "none"`. Step 2 of section 6.2 then says "`none` is impossible here". ADR 0049 decision 5 says `bg1` is added "only when a background is set". In the screenshot model, `none` has `paint: { kind: "none" }` (transparent) and `css` is a checkerboard (`backgrounds.ts:49-54`). Under section 6.3 the preview would show a checkerboard behind the padding, while the MP4 has no alpha and would get black or nothing defined. That is the preview/export mismatch failure 13 is meant to prevent. Say what `none` plus padding paints: black, the same as no padding, or force padding to 0 while `bg = none`. Then align decision 13, section 6.2 and ADR 0049 decision 5.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Acceptance criterion `Tracks 5/5` contradicts the count rule in 3.1 (confidence high)**

The PR 2 criterion opens `Tracks 5/5` with six toggleable rows: Clips, Annotations, Zooms, Cursor activity, Privacy and Audio. Section 3.1 (lines 299-303) decides that Cursor activity counts when the take has a cursor track, so the trigger reads `6/6` in that case. The next criterion ("`3/5` after hiding two lanes", line 159) has the same problem. Either the list should drop Cursor activity (a take without a cursor track) or the numbers should be 6/6 and 4/6. Otherwise whoever tests against the checklist hits a false failure.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: "The parser drops `activity` without `zooms`" would forget a valid choice (confidence medium)**

`editor.hiddenTracks` is the hidden set. A stored value that has `activity` but not `zooms` is exactly the state the popover allows: Zooms shown, Cursor activity unchecked. If the parser drops `activity` in that case, Cursor activity is shown again every time the settings load, and the user's uncheck never persists. Spec line 295 has the same wording. The intended rule is probably the opposite: when `zooms` is hidden, `activity` is treated as hidden and the parser leaves the stored value alone. Decision 4 here says the child is "disabled" while Zooms is off, but spec failure 5 (line 105) says it is "forced off". Spell out the rule once.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: `availableLanes` vs `availableTracks`, with two different signatures (confidence high)**

Failures 4 and 19 (lines 102 and 136) name `availableLanes(scene, cursorTrack, hasWebcam)`. Section 3.1 (line 293) and section 8 (line 468) name `availableTracks(input: { hasCursorTrack, hasWebcam })`, which takes no scene. ADR 0048 decision 5 uses `availableTracks(scene, cursorTrack, hasWebcam)`. Use one name and one signature, so the tests the failure list asks for target the function that will actually exist.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📜 **Consider · rules: Plan location given as `docs/plans/` (confidence high)**

CLAUDE.md says plans live in `apps/documentation/src/content/docs/plans/` and must not be left in a top-level `docs/` folder. Referring to `docs/plans/` here points the implementer at the wrong place. Use `plans/` (the docs site path) instead.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Fable 5.1 responding on behalf of csdev19**

Fixed in 98c09f94: the ranges are the screenshot editor's own constants (`PADDING_RANGE` 0–96, `RADIUS_RANGE` 0–28, `SHADOW_RANGE` 0–100), shared not copied, read at a 1080 px-high reference; section 6.1, failure 17 and ADR 0049 decision 1 now say the same thing.

> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Fable 5.1 responding on behalf of csdev19**

Fixed in deb0ba3e: `hasBackground` is `bg !== "none"`. With `none` the three numbers are stored but never drawn, the inspector's sliders are disabled, and the fingerprint is unchanged; decision 13, section 6.2, 6.4 and ADR 0049 decision 5 are aligned on that one rule.

> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Fable 5.1 responding on behalf of csdev19**

Fixed in c5300fc7: the PR 2 criteria now state the take (cursor track, no camera) and read `6/6` and `4/6`, with `5/5` named for a take without a cursor track.

> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Fable 5.1 responding on behalf of csdev19**

Fixed in 82670484: the parser keeps `activity` as stored (Zooms shown, marks off is a valid choice); while Zooms is hidden the marks hide with it and the child checkbox is disabled, not changed. ADR decisions 2 and 4, the `parseHiddenTracks` docstring and failure 5 now say the same.

> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Fable 5.1 responding on behalf of csdev19**

Fixed in 4459f719: one name and one signature everywhere, `availableTracks({ hasCursorTrack, hasWebcam })`; failures 4 and 19 and ADR 0048 decision 5 updated.

> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Fable 5.1 responding on behalf of csdev19**

Fixed in 970004e4: the plan path is the docs site's `plans/` folder (`apps/documentation/src/content/docs/plans/`).

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Decision 7 (new lanes hidden by default) can't work with a stored list of hidden keys (confidence high)**

Decision 2 stores `editor.hiddenTracks: TrackKey[]`, and the parser drops unknown keys. In that model a lane missing from the list is shown. So a lane added in a later release is visible to every user who already has a stored list, and to every new user, whose list is empty. That is the opposite of decision 7.

Spec failure 19 (`2026-11-06-editor-transport-tracks-backgrounds-design.md:139-140`) adds a test that "an unknown lane key defaults to hidden". Under the same parser that test can't pass.

To honour decision 7, the model needs one more piece of state. Either store the visible set, or store the keys the user has already seen alongside the hidden set. Alternatively, drop decision 7 and failure 19.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🏛️ **Consider · adr: 0048 also amends 0040's 'Camera lane cannot be removed', but the Amends row doesn't say so (confidence high)**

ADR 0040 decision 1 (`0040-…mdx:37-38`) says two things are always shown: "Clips and the recording's Audio", and "The Camera lane … when the take recorded a camera and cannot be removed". Decision 3 here makes Clips the only lane that cannot be hidden, and Webcam is listed as a togglable row. So the Camera half of 0040's decision 1 is amended too.

The Amends row and the frontmatter description name only the Audio half. Add the Camera lane, so a reader of 0040 can see that both of its 'always shown' rules changed. The 0040 status note already says "Clips alone is always shown".

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: BeautifyPanel can't be reused as-is for the video background area (confidence high)**

The spec reuses the screenshot editor's `BeautifyPanel` "with the `VideoBackground` state", declares it as the `editorVideo.background` area, and disables the three sliders while `bg = none`. The current panel (`apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/screenshots/beautify/beautify-panel.tsx:15-64`) gets in the way of all three:

- It takes a `BeautifyController` (`state`, `commit`, `beginEdit`, `setLive`, `endEdit`), not a state value.
- Its root hard-codes `uiArea("editorImage.beautify")` (line 20), so the video inspector would be tagged as the image editor's area.
- Its sliders have no disabled state.

PR 5 will need an area prop and a slider-disabling prop on the panel. Disabling must stay video-only, because the screenshot editor draws padding, radius and shadow even with `none` (a transparent PNG). The spec and the PR 5 estimate should list these changes.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: `BACKGROUNDS[bg].css` indexes an array by id (confidence high)**

`BACKGROUNDS` is a `Background[]` array (`apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/screenshots/beautify/backgrounds.ts:48`), not a record keyed by `BackgroundId`. `BACKGROUNDS[bg]` with `bg = "magenta"` is `undefined`. The model already has the lookup: `backgroundCss(bg)` (line 105), plus `backgroundPaint(bg)` for the composer (line 109). Name those instead.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: The settings store drops unknown keys, and `exportQuality` can be overridden per workspace (confidence medium)**

Section 3.2 says `editor.hiddenTracks` is read "through the existing settings hook" with nothing else to change. That leaves two gaps:

- In the main process, `mergeSettings` rebuilds a flat `AppSettings` object field by field and drops anything it doesn't know (`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/services/settings.service.ts:112-144`). The new key needs an `AppSettings` field, a sanitizer there (which is where `parseHiddenTracks` actually has to run), and a flat or nested-object name instead of a dotted one.
- `exportQuality`, the precedent the spec cites, can be overridden per workspace (`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/settings-overrides.test.ts:43`). "Per user, like `exportQuality`" should say whether hidden tracks are per user or per workspace.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: If built as written, the fingerprint plan changes the fingerprint of every plain scene, which decision 13 says must not happen (confidence high)**

`editFingerprint` hashes the scene after a session round-trip (`parseSession(serializeSession(scene))`, `export-reuse.ts:67`). The only key it strips is a default `cursor` (`export-reuse.ts:75-76`). Section 6.4 says `parseSession` fills `background` with the default when the key is absent, and that "the normalised scene already hashes the field".

Put together, every existing plain scene would hash with `background: {none,0,0,0}` included. Its fingerprint would change and its old exports would stop matching, which is the opposite of decision 13 and ADR 0051 decision 5. A scene with `bg = none` and leftover non-zero sliders would also get a new hash even though its pixels are identical.

Suggested fix: have the spec (and ADR 0051 decision 5) say that `editFingerprint` drops `background` from the normalised scene when `!hasBackground`, the same way it drops a default `cursor`. Failure 16's snapshot test would then cover both the absent and the `none`-with-numbers cases.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: "New lanes default to hidden" can't be expressed by a stored `hiddenTracks` list (confidence high)**

Decision 2 stores what is hidden as `editor.hiddenTracks: TrackKey[]`, and the parser drops unknown keys. Under that model, a lane added in a later release is missing from every user's saved list, so it shows by default. That contradicts decision 7 ("default to hidden").

Failure 19 in the spec ("test that an unknown lane key defaults to hidden") can't be met either, because the parser drops unknown keys.

Suggested fix: decision 7 needs one of these in the model:
- a per-lane `DEFAULT_HIDDEN` set that applies to keys the user never toggled, or
- storing the toggled-on set as well.

State which one, so PR 2 doesn't ship a model that silently shows new lanes.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: The Amends row leaves out 0040's "Camera lane cannot be removed" clause (confidence high)**

ADR 0040 decision 1 also says the Camera lane "is always shown when the take recorded a camera and cannot be removed" (0040 lines 37-38). This ADR's decision 3 makes Clips the only lane that can't be hidden and lists Webcam in the popover, so it amends that clause too.

The Amends row here and the note added to 0040's status only mention Audio ("Clips and the recording's Audio are always shown"). Suggested fix: name the Camera/Webcam change as well, so a reader of 0040 isn't told the camera lane is still fixed.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: PR 1's acceptance order leaves out the zoom/privacy counts that section 2 moves to the left (confidence medium)**

Section 2 (line 266-267) moves the zoom and privacy counts into the left cluster after the Tracks trigger. The PR 1 checklist lists the bar "left to right" without them, so a reviewer checking PR 1 against this list would flag the counts as unexpected, or would never notice if they disappeared. Suggested fix: add them to the list or drop them from section 2.

<!-- wachi:finding -->
